meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; unitary national system with no sub-state tax distinction) heavily overlaid by EU-derived commercial, food-safety, and AML/CFT regulations

OECD Multilateral Instrument / BEPS MLI (France: in force 1 January 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50, L.561-2-2 and L.561-46 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF); Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on transfers of funds; TRACFIN doctrine and ACPR AML/KYC guidelines
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs — RBE; following CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20, general public access is restricted; access is granted to French supervisory authorities, TRACFIN, DG Trésor and AML-obliged entities demonstrating legitimate interest; no nominee-friendly public registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or statutory representative in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority; utility provider of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised true-copy certification; apostille where required by bank KYC policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) granted to the incorporation signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the grantor's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization; reviewed at incorporation and bank onboarding

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of all non-French corporate, constitutional and identity documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's certification annexed to apostilled originals

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory standard due diligence at onboarding: screen all shareholders, UBOs, directors and signatories at the 25% threshold or control positions against (i) TRACFIN/DG Trésor French asset-freeze list (fichier des avoirs gelés), (ii) UN Consolidated Sanctions (1267/1988 and 1988/2233 regimes), (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions (Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and associated lists), (iv) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists for USD Swift_LC/TT_Wire clearing, and (v) national FICOBA and ACPR impaired-compliance records. Enhanced due diligence with source-of-funds verification applies to any PEP regardless of the Low_Risk_Standard tier; ongoing monitoring with list refresh at least every 24 months and on adverse-media alerts.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr — single official e-filing window); name availability search via Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) and INPI Data (data.inpi.fr); official publication at BODACC and in an approved legal gazette (Journal d'annonces légales)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statuts and all public filings (M0 form, Kbis extract) must be executed in French; under Loi Toubon n° 94-665 and Article L.123-1-4 of the Code de commerce, the corporate name must be in Latin script and acceptable in French judicial notation; foreign-language names are permissible if transliterated into Latin characters and not contrary to public order or misleading to consumers
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (regulated credit-activity term — requires prior ACPR or ministerial authorisation)
Assurance / Insurance (regulated term — requires prudential authorisation)
Crédit / Prêt / Finance (sensitive financial tokens triggering regulatory review)
France / National / République (misleading territorial or sovereign indications requiring ministerial consent)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross (protected emblems under Geneva Conventions law)
Biologique / Bio (controlled organic claim requiring AB certification under EU Regulation 2018/848)
Terms contrary to public order, morality, or infringing prior trademark rights (L.711-1 et seq. Code de la propriété intellectuelle)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_validity_note: France does not operate a standalone 30-day name-reservation system; the Greffe de Paris performs an availability and identity check on the day of filing (M0 dossier) and the name becomes protected upon RCS registration and Kbis issuance. For durable exclusivity, a trademark application at INPI is recommended (10-year renewable protection, official fee EUR 190 for the first class plus EUR 40 per additional class).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Greffier du tribunal de commerce refuses the corporate name (e.g., for identity with an earlier RCS registration or misleading character), the applicant may (i) file a formal re-examination request with the same Greffe within 8 days, (ii) submit a revised name through the Guichet des Formalités, or (iii) initiate proceedings before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal Judiciaire de Paris for judicial registration. For trademark-based refusals by INPI, the statutory opposition window is 2 months from publication under Article L.712-4 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle, followed by appeal to the Cour d'appel within 1 month of the INPI decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The SAS legal seat (siège social) may validly be domiciled at the President's residence or with an approved domiciliation company (Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-137 Code de commerce) for up to 5 years (renewable). However, for an aseptic UHT barista oat-milk plant, a purely virtual accommodation is NOT commercially or regulatory acceptable for production substance: completion of the entity requires a physical industrial plant with (i) prior activity declaration to DDPP/DGCCRF under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, (ii) ICPE environmental registration/authorisation (rubrique 2220 — industries de transformation de matières végétales), and (iii) HACCP and aseptic packaging GMP compliance. French banks, BPI France, EU trade buyers and export insurance providers all condition disbursement and LC confirmations on evidence of the physical plant and its sanitary approvals.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 85% probability of at least one unannounced DGCCRF/DDPP hygiene, traceability and metrology inspection during the first 12 months of UHT plant operation, plus ICPE environmental compliance visits; inspection intensity increases when the plant registers for EU export and private-label retail supply contracts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 concerning sociétés par actions simplifiées; Articles L.123-1 et seq. concerning the Register of Commerce and Companies; Articles L.561-46 et seq. concerning beneficial-owner filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online declaration of company incorporation (déclaration de constitution or formalité de création) submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, accompanied by the signed SAS articles of association and beneficial-owner declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The articles must state the capital amount and subscribed shares. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation; the balance may be paid within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must generally be fully paid upon issuance. A French bank account may be opened for the capital deposit, and the depositary issues a certificate of deposit. The capital may be released after registration. The stated fee is an indicative USD equivalent of the principal commercial-registration charge; registry, beneficial-owner, legal-notice, banking, translation, and publication charges may apply separately and vary by tariff and exchange rate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscription of its entire issued share capital as set out in the subscription schedule and articles of association, and that the President is authorised to receive and verify the capital deposit certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address] and adopted as the Company’s registered office from incorporation. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed President for an indefinite term, with authority to represent the Company in accordance with law and the articles. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Directeur Général, if applicable, with the powers specified in the articles. The President is authorised to complete all filing and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure, activities, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique; relevant mairie and commercial court registry for address and local-use verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS form, shareholding, capital, voting rights, President, optional Directeur Général, principal activity, and French registered office. Verify that the premises may be used as a registered office and that the proposed activity is compatible with zoning and lease restrictions. Obtain a domiciliation agreement, commercial lease, or proof of ownership. Foreign corporate shareholders should provide legalized or apostilled corporate extracts and certified French translations where required.
required_dossiers: Registered-office title, lease, or domiciliation certificate
Description of the principal and ancillary activities
Foreign shareholder corporate certificates and powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the address, activity code, or supporting evidence requested by the INPI or registry. Replace non-compliant domiciliation evidence and resubmit through the same electronic formalities file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and appointed professional advisers; no general notarial execution is required for ordinary cash incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare articles stating the name, form, capital, share classes, contributions, transfer restrictions, governance powers, fiscal year, registered office, duration, dissolution rules, and conditions for collective decisions. Execute the articles electronically or in original form. A notarial deed is required where real estate is contributed or where another legally protected transaction requires notarisation. Obtain a commissaire aux apports report for in-kind contributions unless the statutory exemption conditions are validly satisfied.
required_dossiers: Final SAS articles signed by all subscribers
In-kind contribution valuation report, or valid waiver documentation
Directeur Général acceptance statement, if appointed
Power of attorney for filing representative, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend defective provisions, obtain missing signatures or acceptance statements, and execute a corrected version before filing. If an in-kind contribution is challenged, commission an independent contribution auditor and amend the capital documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the capital-deposit account and fund subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, payment institution, or other legally authorised depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed articles, draft incorporation documents, identification documents, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, and banking mandate. Transfer the subscribed cash capital from the subscriber’s account. Obtain the capital-deposit certificate identifying the company under formation, the amount received, and the depositary. Do not treat the certificate as evidence of full payment where only the required minimum has been deposited.
required_dossiers: Signed articles or certified draft articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC queries with certified ownership, tax-residence, source-of-funds, and business-purpose evidence. If the bank declines onboarding, use another authorised depositary and preserve the complete audit trail.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised legal-notices publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish an avis de constitution containing the legal form, company name, capital, registered office, principal activity, duration, President, and relevant governance information required for an SAS. Use an authorised journal or approved online legal-notices service. Obtain the publication certificate and ensure that the notice is consistent with the articles and INPI filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Publish a corrective notice if the legal-notices service or registry identifies a material omission or inconsistency. Retain both the original and corrective publication certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation and beneficial-owner filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, transmitting the file to the competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic creation form, select the SAS legal form, provide the principal activity and establishment details, upload the articles, publication certificate, capital-deposit certificate, office evidence, officer declarations, identification documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the applicable electronic filing charges. Sign using the required authentication method and retain the filing receipt and tracking number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of publication of the legal notice
President and officer identity and non-conviction declarations
Contribution auditor report or exemption statement, if applicable
Foreign documents with apostille or legalisation and French translation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the electronic dashboard and respond within the stated deadline to any request for regularisation. Upload corrected documents through the same file, explain each correction, and preserve the registry correspondence. A rejected filing may be resubmitted after curing the stated defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry; INPI; tax administration and social-security portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the extrait Kbis or current registry extract, SIREN and SIRET numbers, APE activity code, and beneficial-owner filing confirmation. After registration, provide the Kbis to the bank to release deposited capital. Register for VAT and corporate-tax administration as required, establish payroll and social-security accounts before hiring, and maintain statutory registers and accounting records.
required_dossiers: Statutory share register and transfer register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct post-registration data through INPI or the competent registry. Challenge an incorrect APE code or registry entry with supporting evidence and notify the bank, tax authority, and counterparties of corrected information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve governance records and corporate delegations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company President and shareholders; commercial court registry only where a statutory filing is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board or shareholder resolutions permitted by the articles, confirm capital subscription, registered office, officer appointments, bank mandates, accounting engagement, and authority matrix. An SAS has no statutory board unless its articles create one; governance must therefore follow the articles. Record decisions in the applicable decision register and file any change of President, registered office, or beneficial owner through the INPI Guichet unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt a ratifying or corrective resolution, amend the articles where necessary, and file mandatory changes within the statutory period. Preserve evidence that each signatory had authority at the relevant date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Prefect of the department, generally acting through the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), for installations classified under the Installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) regime. The competent mairie, Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP), and other authorities may also be involved.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE authorisation environnementale, ICPE registration (enregistrement), or ICPE declaration, depending on actual capacity and classified activities; for milk-alternative beverage production, the applicable classification must be confirmed against ICPE nomenclature, including potentially Rubrique 2230 for treatment or processing of milk or milk-like products, and ancillary boiler, storage, refrigeration, or waste activities. A building permit and food-establishment regulatory declarations may also be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition environmental authorities, including the DREAL and the competent environmental assessment authority (autorité environnementale), with the Prefect as permitting authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Capacity-dependent. An ICPE registration or declaration may apply below the authorisation threshold; a full environmental authorisation and environmental assessment may apply above the relevant threshold or where project-specific criteria trigger it. The final tier requires verified tonnes-per-day capacity, storage volumes, boiler fuel and thermal power, wastewater discharge route, site sensitivity, and cumulative activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: There is no single universal wastewater threshold for every oat-beverage plant. Discharge limits must be stated in the ICPE order or municipal sewer agreement and commonly address flow, pH, temperature, suspended solids, biological oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, nitrogen, phosphorus, fats, oils, and cleaning chemicals. Direct discharges require applicable water-law and ICPE authorisation. Indirect discharges require prior sewer-operator approval. VOC, combustion, noise, odour, and air-emission limits are activity- and equipment-specific and may derive from the ICPE order and the Arrêté ministériel of 2 February 1998, where applicable. Hazardous and non-hazardous waste must be segregated, characterised, stored safely, transferred to authorised operators, and tracked through required waste records and digital tracking systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the applicable building permit and, where relevant, approval for an établissement recevant du public or industrial premises from the mairie and fire-safety authorities, including consultation with the Service départemental d'incendie et de secours (SDIS). Complete fire-compartmentation, emergency access, alarm, extinguishing, evacuation, and hazardous-material controls. Commission structural-load, machinery, electrical, pressure-equipment, refrigeration, and lifting-equipment inspections where applicable. Before operations and hiring, implement the occupational-risk assessment document (DUERP), machine safeguarding, chemical and cleaning-agent controls, food-safety procedures, occupational health arrangements, workplace training, and required labour and social-security registrations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a presence in France must register with the DGFiP to obtain a SIREN/SIRET identification number and VAT identification number (FR followed by 11 digits); the procedure requires submission of incorporation documents, proof of registered office address, detailed business activity description, and payment of registration fees through the guichet unique or direct DGFiP channels
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections are available under French law; all French SAS entities are subject to mandatory entity-level taxation under the Impôt sur les Sociétés regime

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 85,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) for qualifying B2B transactions with digital stamping and clearance enforced through API integration with the French tax authorities

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside the European Union or services performed for non-EU clients qualify for 0% VAT rate, substantiated by export documentation and proof of non-repatriation of VAT
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating may result in penalties up to 80 percent of the evaded VAT amount, retrospective clawback of zero-rated transactions, and potential criminal prosecution under French tax legislation

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital account and current account convertibility under EU free movement of capital rules. Profit remittances face no significant regulatory hurdles for resident French SAS entities; beneficial ownership and transaction reporting to the Banque de France or ACPR may apply for transactions above reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted freely to EUR. Statutory requirements include customs declarations and potential VAT reporting; no conversion ratios or surrender timelines apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited feasibility for offshore digital EMIs due to French banking regulations and AML requirements; onshore corporate accounts preferred for cross-border operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video interviews permitted for directors and signatories; physical presence required only for account opening, notarization, or high-value transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening or beneficial ownership verification failure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extracts, beneficial ownership register, source of funds documentation, and director identification

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'INV' for investments; verification through KYC, beneficial ownership disclosure, and source of funds confirmation prior to processing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing via SWIFT MT103 for trade settlements or issuance of commercial letters of credit (LCs) through correspondent banks; all transactions subject to French export controls and anti-money laundering monitoring.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; no separate filing authority for approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval within six months after the financial year-end; convening notice and information must comply with the SAS articles and applicable Commercial Code requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential judicial injunction to approve accounts, director liability, and a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; no automatic fixed-time strike-off rule applies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet unique managed by INPI, with registration through the competent commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval, or within two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing, civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, possible director liability, and potential administrative or judicial removal from the register after formal notices; France has no standard automatic annual strike-off timetable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second working day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar and any officially published extensions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge, increasing in aggravated cases; additional assessment, penalties, and tax audit exposure may apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation and final VAT return, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: According to the applicable VAT regime; annual regularisation is generally submitted with the final periodic VAT return or annual CA12 return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, late-filing surcharge generally starting at 10%, assessed VAT, and potential penalties for inaccurate or omitted declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet unique and the French register of beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing is required; changes must generally be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, court-ordered compliance, criminal or civil sanctions for inaccurate or omitted information, and potential restrictions or consequences affecting the entity's registration status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Lower thresholds and additional rules may apply to companies controlled by another company or forming part of a qualifying group. Appointment may also be required by the articles, shareholders, court order, or applicable group rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) rules; IFRS is generally used for qualifying consolidated accounts and may be permitted or required in specific regulated circumstances

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual UBO confirmation filing. The SAS must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information and report each qualifying change, including changes in control or beneficial ownership, generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be documented in the transfer records, shareholder accounts, and applicable corporate resolutions or approvals without waiting for an annual filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholder accounts and share transfers
Register of shareholders or equivalent shareholder identification records
Register of beneficial owners and supporting identification records
Minute book or secure record of shareholder decisions and corporate decisions
Register or file of statutory auditor appointments and reports, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,700 per year, depending on location, mail handling, legal representation, and compliance support; France does not impose a general annual registered-agent renewal fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,300-16,500 for a small or medium SAS, depending on turnover, transaction volume, group reporting, inventory procedures, internal controls, and consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate in France, plus applicable social contribution of 3.3% for companies whose corporate income tax exceeds EUR 763,000 and whose annual revenue is at least EUR 7.63 million, producing a combined marginal rate of approximately 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to annual revenue not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by qualifying individuals or qualifying entities. Research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory conditions. Patent and qualifying intellectual-property income may generally benefit from a separate 10% rate under the nexus approach. No general statutory tax holiday applies to an ordinary SAS operating an oat-milk manufacturing plant.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration professional portal espace professionnel on impots.gouv.fr using EFI or through an accredited EDI-TDFC provider. The annual tax return is accompanied principally by forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD and the tax balance-sheet and income-statement schedules 2050-SD through 2057-SD. Forms 2065 and the tax schedules are generally filed electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return. Corporate income tax instalments are generally payable quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with a final balance generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the fiscal year-end or, for a 31 December year-end, by 15 May.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May, subject to the tax administration's annually published calendar and electronic-filing extensions. A newly incorporated SAS must file for its first accounting period by the deadline applicable to the period-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year beginning and ending dates, principal activity, and legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS as the taxpayer. Identify the foreign parent only where requested for ownership, related-party, tax-consolidation, or payment information. A non-resident shareholder is not itself substituted for the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation limitations, provisions, tax credits, and other French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the French SAS's taxable result, including income attributable to its French operations. Do not deduct foreign-head-office charges unless they satisfy French deductibility, allocation, documentation, and arm's-length requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss through add-backs and deductions, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, participation-exemption adjustments, and tax-credit adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose adjustments for cross-border royalties, interest, management fees, inventory transfers, and other related-party transactions. Unsupported or excessive charges are exposed to transfer-pricing and profit-diversion adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report current-year losses, carried-forward losses used, and remaining losses. Loss carryforward is generally unlimited in duration but subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year profit exceeding EUR 1 million; a carryback election is limited and subject to statutory conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally incurred by the French SAS. Foreign-parent or foreign-subsidiary losses cannot be imported absent a specific French tax-consolidation or reorganization rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax credits, group transactions, participation-related items, shareholdings, capital gains, and other statutory reconciliation information applicable to the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose qualifying foreign related-party holdings, intragroup restructurings, dividend receipts, and cross-border disposals. Apply participation exemption and treaty positions only where ownership, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, payables, cash, equity, and expense details supporting the tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts must reconcile with the SAS statutory accounts and general ledger. Foreign-currency transactions must be translated under French accounting and tax rules, with supporting intercompany invoices and payment evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report corporate income tax credits, instalments, tax withheld, tax-consolidation information, and the final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign tax credits only where available under French law or an applicable tax treaty. Treaty relief does not automatically authorize a credit for foreign tax that is not legally creditable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide required information concerning controlled transactions, related entities, methods, amounts, and documentation. Certain groups must file a summary transfer-pricing declaration, generally Form 2257-SD, and qualifying multinational groups must file a country-by-country report or notification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report transactions with foreign parent companies, affiliates, procurement entities, licensors, lenders, and service companies. Maintain a French Local File and, where applicable, a Master File and country-by-country reporting package.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, calculated under the applicable statutory rules; France does not generally impose a separate automatic daily surcharge for ordinary corporate income tax filing delay. Failure to use mandatory electronic filing may trigger a penalty generally equal to 0.2% of the relevant amount, subject to statutory minimums. Tax audits may also produce reassessed tax, interest, penalties, transfer-pricing adjustments, and criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive regime may provide a 0% exemption for a qualifying EU or European Economic Area corporate parent meeting ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse requirements. French domestic participation exemption generally applies to qualifying dividends received by a French corporate shareholder, with a taxable add-back of 1% or 5% depending on the regime and ownership relationship.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the applicable French treaty form, principally Form 5000-SD, certified by the recipient's foreign tax authority, together with Form 5001-SD for dividends, Form 5002-SD for interest, or Form 5003-SD for royalties where applicable. The French payer must verify residence, beneficial ownership, entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test requirements, and anti-abuse conditions, then apply the reduced rate only where legally supportable. If full withholding was made, the non-resident generally seeks a refund from the French tax administration using the certified forms and payment evidence within the applicable limitation period. Treaty relief is unavailable where the recipient is an agent, conduit, artificial arrangement, or otherwise fails the treaty's anti-abuse requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction, EU interest-and-royalties relief, and statutory exemptions. Interest paid by a French debtor to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, except in specified cases, including payments to residents of non-cooperative states or territories, where a 75% rate may apply. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and interest withholding to approximately 0% to 15%, but the applicable bilateral treaty, beneficial ownership, debt characterization, anti-abuse rules, and recipient residence must be verified. Payments to related parties must also satisfy French transfer-pricing and interest-deduction limitations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets generally triggers the full French transfer-pricing documentation obligation, including Local File and Master File requirements, subject to statutory extension rules for certain controlled groups. A country-by-country report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. French entities below the full-documentation threshold must still apply the arm's-length principle and maintain documentation adequate to substantiate material controlled transactions. A transfer-pricing summary declaration, generally Form 2257-SD, may apply independently of the full-documentation threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to the United Arab Emirates ESR regime. Nevertheless, French anti-abuse rules, the general abuse-of-law doctrine, treaty principal-purpose tests, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, interest-limitation rules, anti-diversion rules, and transfer-pricing provisions require genuine commercial substance. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, manufacturing capacity, personnel, premises, production records, inventory control, commercial risks, financing evidence, and contemporaneous board and management records consistent with its claimed functions. A low-substance French entity receiving substantial royalties, management fees, financing income, or entrepreneurial margins is a high-risk audit profile.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating expenses, falsifying inventory, maintaining parallel accounts, deliberately understating taxable profit, or knowingly filing materially false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, recovery of unpaid tax, late-payment interest, and penalties generally up to 80% for fraudulent conduct. Criminal tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years and an individual fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated sanctions potentially reaching 7 years and EUR 3 million in specified serious cases, including organized fraud or use of accounts or entities abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, director-disqualification measures, personal tax liability in cases of fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct under the French Tax Code, and civil restitution. Corporate criminal fines can be multiplied under French criminal law. A general automatic travel ban does not arise solely from a tax assessment, but judicial control, passport restrictions, asset-freezing, or detention may apply in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, procurement fees, interest, or product prices to shift French manufacturing profit to a foreign affiliate; failing to document functions, assets, risks, or comparables; or using a loss-making French entity without commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable income may be increased under the French abnormal act of management and transfer-pricing rules. The reassessment may include withholding tax, interest, a 10% or higher penalty, up to 40% for deliberate non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent conduct. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a separate penalty generally calculated by reference to the higher of a statutory minimum or 0.5% of the transactions covered by missing documentation, subject to statutory limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for knowingly approving non-arm's-length arrangements, criminal liability if the conduct forms part of tax fraud, and personal tax-liability proceedings for fraudulent or seriously negligent management. Repeated failures may support management disqualification and asset-preservation measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial shell company, conduit, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SAS with no real employees, premises, production capacity, decision-making, inventory, or commercial risk to obtain treaty benefits, manufacture deductible charges, route royalties, or create artificial residence or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty benefits, deductions, exemptions, and tax credits may be denied under French anti-abuse rules, the abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, and treaty principal-purpose tests. Reassessed tax may be increased by penalties of 40% for deliberate abuse and 80% for fraudulent abuse, in addition to interest and potential withholding-tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil restitution, tax-liability proceedings, criminal liability where fraud is established, and management bans. A shell company is not unlawful solely because it has foreign owners or limited staffing, but artificiality combined with tax evasion, false invoicing, or money laundering materially increases personal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared cross-border payments and withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, commissions, or other reportable amounts to foreign recipients without applying required withholding, relying on uncertified treaty forms, or failing to report payment recipients and amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SAS may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, filing penalties, and penalties for deliberate or fraudulent non-compliance. The payer generally cannot rely on an informal residence certificate where the statutory treaty-relief documentation and beneficial-ownership conditions are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be pursued for management fault, fraudulent withholding-tax avoidance, or participation in tax fraud. Civil and criminal consequences may include restitution, fines, management disqualification, asset freezing, and imprisonment where the conduct satisfies criminal tax or money-laundering offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, illicit funds, and AML failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained capital, circular intercompany loans, false trade invoices, concealed beneficial ownership, payments through high-risk intermediaries, or transfers inconsistent with the plant's commercial activity; failing to identify customers, suppliers, ultimate beneficial owners, or suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is generally punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 375,000, with aggravated cases generally punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 750,000. Corporate entities may face substantially higher criminal fines, confiscation, dissolution in severe cases, and regulatory sanctions for AML-control failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation, civil restitution, management bans, judicial restrictions, and asset freezing. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court in criminal proceedings but are not an automatic consequence of an AML compliance deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating production volumes, inventory, invoices, purchase orders, quality records, or intercompany balances; concealing liabilities; or preparing accounts that do not give a true and fair representation of the SAS's financial position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may face tax reassessment, accounting and commercial-law penalties, criminal fines, confiscation, and possible dissolution for serious offenses. False accounting may support separate fraud, forgery, use-of-false-document, or tax-evasion charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, directors, finance officers, and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, civil damages, creditor claims, management disqualification, personal liability for insufficient assets in insolvency proceedings, and imprisonment where the facts satisfy the applicable offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Deduction of non-business or insufficiently documented expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deducting shareholder expenses, personal benefits, unsupported management charges, excessive executive compensation, non-arm's-length financing costs, or expenses unrelated to the French oat-milk production business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The expense may be denied, taxable income increased, and related withholding or social taxes assessed. Deliberate or fraudulent conduct may attract penalties of up to 40% or 80%, together with interest and possible criminal tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for restitution or tax debts where the expense reflects fraudulent or seriously negligent management. Improper distributions may also create repayment claims against recipients and liability under French corporate and insolvency rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT and excise-related fraud connected with food manufacturing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting domestic sales, claiming input VAT on fictitious purchases, misclassifying plant-based beverages, using false export evidence, or applying an incorrect VAT rate to products or packaging transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on conduct, denial of input-credit claims, and potential criminal prosecution for organized or fraudulent conduct. Product classification and applicable VAT treatment must be verified against the exact product composition, packaging, and sales channel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal tax liability for fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct, criminal liability for intentional fraud, civil restitution, management bans, and asset-preservation measures.
